{{short description|Swiss marine biologist (1922-2003)}}
'''Katharina Maria Mangold-Wirz''' (23 May 1922 - 22 November 2003) was a [[Swiss people|Swiss]] [[marine biologist]] and [[malacologist]] who worked at [[Université Pierre et Marie Curie]]'s [[Observatoire océanologique de Banyuls-sur-Mer|Laboratoire Arago]] in [[Banyuls-sur-Mer]], France.<ref name = PETYmol>{{cite web | url = https://www.bemon.loven.gu.se/petymol.m.html | title = Biographical Etymology of Marine Organism Names. M | access-date = 25 February 2018 | publisher = Hans.G.Hansson}}</ref>

Mangold-Wirz was born Katharina Maria Wirz on 23 May 1922 in [[Basel]] to Eduard Wirz (1891–1970), a teacher, historian and writer, and Clara Wirz-Burgin. She graduated from high school in Basel in 1940 and went to [[Basel University]] to study medicine with the ambition of being a [[brain surgeon]]. Specialists in Switzerland discouraged her from pursuing this ambition as she was "too short, female and appeared frail!" She switched to studying [[zoology]] from 1943 to 1948, achieving a D.Phil. with her thesis on non-human brains supervised by [[Adolf Portmann]] and published in 1950 in ''[[Acta Anatomica]]''. She was awarded a 3-year scholarship at the Janggen-Pöhn Foundation of [[St Gallen]] to carry out research on [[Opisthobranchs]] from 1950 in [[Villefranche-sur-Mer]] and Banyuls-sur-Mer. In 1951 she was appointed as a researcher at the [[Centre National de la Recherché Scientifique]] and her focus from then was on the biology of [[cephalopods]]. Portmann was her mentor until he died in 1982.<ref name = Allcock>{{cite journal | author-link1 = Louise Allcock |author1=Louise M. Allcock | author2 = Sigurd Von Boletzky | author3 = Laure Bonnaud | author4 = Erica A. G. Vidal | year = 2015 | title = The role of female cephalopod researchers: past and present | url = https://hal.science/hal-02141733/document | journal = Journal of Natural History | volume = 49 | issue = 21–24 | pages = 1235–1266 | doi=10.1080/00222933.2015.1037088| s2cid = 86871267 | url-access =  | url-status =  | archive-url =  | archive-date =  }}</ref>

In 1958 she married Walter Mangold, in 1961 was awarded the {{lang|fr|Doctorat ès Sciences}} ({{lang|fr|Doctorat d'état}}) from the [[University of Paris]], and had her thesis published in {{lang|fr|Vie et Meileu}}. In that year she was also promoted to Research Fellow at the Centre National de la Recherché Scientifique, and in 1966 she was appointed as a Senior Researcher. In 1969 overseas recognition came with her appointment as a visiting Research Professor at the [[Memorial University of Newfoundland]]. Further recognition came in 1983 when she was elected as the first president of the [[Cephalopod International Advisory Council]] at their meeting in Banyuls-sur-Mer. She continued as an active scientist after retiring from academia in 1987. In 1989 she co-authored the cephalopod volume of the [[textbook]] with Grassé, {{lang|fr|Traité du Zoologie}} and in 1993 was appointed an honorary life member of the Cephalopod International Advisory Council. She died in Basel on 22 November 2003.<ref name = Allcock/>

The octopus ''[[Microeledone mangoldi]]''<ref name = Allcock/> and the squid ''[[Asperoteuthis mangoldae]]'' are named in her honour.<ref name = Young>{{cite journal | author-link1 = Richard E. Young | author1 = R.E. Young | author-link2 = Michael Vecchione | author2 = M. Vecchione | author-link3 = Clyde Roper | author3 = C. F. E. Roper | year = 2007 | title = A new genus and three new species of decapodiform cephalopods (Mollusca: Cephalopoda) | url = https://repository.si.edu/bitstream/handle/10088/6235/Young_2007_a_new_genus_and_three_n.pdf | journal = Reviews in Fish Biology and Fisheries | volume = 17 | issue =2–3 | pages = 353–365 | doi=10.1007/s11160-007-9044-z| s2cid = 35493476 }}</ref>
